claims.claim: Author started using Disqus in 2018 when it was arguably the leading commenting system
claims.quote: I started using Disqus in 2018.

claims.claim: Disqus began showing ads on author's blog in January 2021
claims.quote: in January 2021, Disqus started polluting my blog with unwanted ads

claims.claim: Disqus charges $10/month per site to remove ads
claims.quote: Disqus is charging a monthly fee of $10/month per site to remove its own imposed ads

claims.claim: Change affects many small businesses and bloggers relying on Disqus
claims.quote: This change affects a large number of small businesses and bloggers

claims.claim: Giscus is an open-source commenting system relying on GitHub Discussions
claims.quote: open-source commenting system that relies on GitHub Discussions

claims.claim: Tweet from Feb 2017 complains Disqus forces ads that pay nothing
claims.quote: These ads pay nothing & they force them.

claims.claim: Number of comments is an accurate measure of publication popularity (author's view)
claims.quote: the number of comments is an accurate measure of the popularity of a publication

claims.claim: Moderating comments consumes considerable time
claims.quote: moderating visitor comments can consume a considerable amount of time

claims.claim: Disqus offers ad removal for an inexpensive monthly fee
claims.quote: For an inexpensive monthly fee publishers will be able to completely remove ads

claims.claim: Author calls the ad-removal fee a bad move for small blogs
claims.quote: This is a bad move from Disqus, especially for small blogs

claims.claim: Disqus ads cover large screen portion and tend to be click bait or fake news
claims.quote: They cover a large portion of the screen and tend to be either click bait or fake news.

claims.claim: Disqus degrades page load time via comment syncing and third-party ad scripts
claims.quote: Disqus is know to degrade page load time.

claims.claim: Disqus forces visitors to log in with social accounts, raising privacy issues
claims.quote: forcing visitors to log in with their social media accounts when commenting

claims.claim: Giscus preferred; supports replies since built on GitHub discussions
claims.quote: It relies on GitHub discussions, which means that it supports replies

claims.claim: Utterances is built on GitHub Issues, widely used, may flood repo issues over time
claims.quote: given enough time, it might flood your repository's issues with comments

claims.claim: Gitalk based on GitHub Issues and Preact; has distraction free mode, hotkeys, localization
claims.quote: Facebook-like distraction free mode, hotkeys, and automatic language localization

claims.claim: GitHub-based solutions suit developer-skewed audiences with GitHub accounts
claims.quote: ideal for sites with an audience that skews towards developers

claims.claim: Blog runs on GitHub Pages with Jekyll, deployed free
claims.quote: I can deploy my website on GitHub completely free

claims.claim: Jekyll is a static site generator created by one of GitHub's founders
claims.quote: Jekyll is a static site generator created by one of the GitHub founders

claims.claim: Giscus uses GitHub Discussions as backing store; supports replies, reactions, easier moderation
claims.quote: supports comments replies, more engaging discussion reactions, and is easier to moderate

claims.claim: Giscus avoids API rate limits, server-side code, manual post-issue linking, and leaving the site
claims.quote: no need to worry about GitHub API rate limits, managing server-side code

claims.claim: Giscus finds discussion via Discussions search API using chosen mapping; bot creates discussion on first comment or reaction
claims.quote: the giscus bot will automatically create a discussion the first time someone leaves a comment or reaction

claims.claim: Commenters must authorize giscus app via GitHub OAuth, or comment on GitHub directly; moderation on GitHub
claims.quote: visitors must authorize the giscus app to post on their behalf using the GitHub OAuth flow

claims.claim: Giscus requires three things: public repo, giscus app installed, Discussions enabled
claims.quote: the GitHub repo has to meet only three requirement

claims.claim: REPO_ID and CATEGORY_ID obtained from Giscus form; theme customizable via CUSTOM_CSS path
claims.quote: The REPO_ID and CATEGORY_ID can be obtained using the Giscus form.

claims.claim: Author overrides font sizes: mr-2 20px, .text-sm 18px, .text-xs 12px
Giscus extra config via .giscus.json in repo root; origins and originsRegex restrict domains loading discussions
claims.quote: restrict the domains that can load this website's repository discussions via giscus

claims.claim: Author config sets defaultCommentOrder to oldest and allows localhost via regex
Author chose Giscus: lightweight, open-source, free, ad-free
claims.quote: I prefer a lightweight, open-source, and free solution for handling my blog comments.

claims.claim: Giscus depends on GitHub (Microsoft), so exposed to future changes; fee for public repos unlikely
claims.quote: it is highly unlikely to expect some sort of fee for public repositories
